reason: Linear target interpolation reduces internal ripple but violates the unchanged 30 Hz tracking_error_rad gate.
original_v2_report_note: v2 observer equivalence boolean referred only to batched versus observed integration, not linear; v3 explicitly lists the compared methods.
comparison_scope: Short approach diagnostic with identical 30 Hz controller inputs and simulation duration. Linear mode changes the internal actuator-target schedule and resulting physics. No attachment, state assignment during motion, video retiming or quality-limit change.
limitations: Short pre-contact reconstruction, not exact historical physics or a complete task.
Missing free-object velocities/warm starts and float32 action storage limit historical reconstruction.
Native substep and 30 Hz finite-difference derivatives use different bandwidths; existing acceptance gates are not reinterpreted.
Solver force/contact buffers are intentionally not assigned post-integration timestamps by this diagnostic.
CPU-only low-priority work on the shared benchmark host; not end-to-end throughput.
No real hardware response, force limit or calibration is established.
next_requirement: Any future controller candidate must pass original closed-loop whole-task motion, contact, release and dataset audits, then be benchmarked separately; short free-space results do not grant production acceptance.
